subject: Re: Acme long-context eval — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Acme long-context eval — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Hi Sara,

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs
- Large documents (~100k tokens) ingestion and extraction (multi-doc summarization, entity extraction across chapters)
- Deterministic extractive summaries for compliance review; high fidelity for citations
- Tight latency target for interactive reviewer flows (~350-500ms p50 for short queries; background batch jobs ok to be higher)

Model fit / initial recommendations
- For best long-context fidelity we recommend testing: 1) Llama-3-70B-ctx (70B base, 128k context if you provision extended KV) and 2) RedSeq-34B-long (optimized for sparse attention + 65k context). 
- Quantized variants (8-bit PTQ) are a strong cost/latency tradeoff; we flag potential small quality regressions vs fp16 which we'll validate in evals.

Benchmarks & eval assets (attached)
- I attached: eval_prompt_set_v1.csv (suggested prompt templates + expected outputs) and redwood-long-context-benchmarks.pdf (sample latency/quality curve for extended-context models). Also sharing our public benchmark page: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/long-context

Quality/regression concerns
- We saw a couple of models trade off citation fidelity when using heavy truncation strategies. Our eval tooling runs a truncation sweep (full, sliding-window, prefix-only) and reports hallucination/citation precision. We recommend running the truncation sweep as part of the first two-week eval window.

Proposed next steps
1) You share the canonical dataset (or subset) and any non-disclosure constraints (I got your note about redactions).
2) We run a 2-week long-context eval (truncation sweep + summarization fidelity tests) against the two recommended models and their quantized variants.
3) Share results, pick a canary policy (model variant + fallback) and rollout plan.

Can you confirm: 1) the sample corpus we discussed (10 documents, ~1M tokens total) is available and 2) if Acme wants on-prem/Private evaluation or hosted with dedicated capacity?

Thanks, looping in Lauren (product) and Michael (ML infra) for rollout/quantization planning.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood-long-context-benchmarks.pdf

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of quick questions before we lock the eval: 

1) Latency: you recommend the Llama-3-70B-ctx but we're worried about meeting the interactive p50 target when using 128k KV. Do you have examples of p50 numbers for a 2-4 token response path on dedicated GPUs?
2) Hallucination / regression: last year we saw a regression after a quantized rollout (higher hallucination on citation tasks). What regression controls do you run?
3) Truncation behavior: how do you handle very long sequences for extractive QA vs summarization? Is there a single best-practice or will it be model-specific?

I attached our evaluation spec (acme-eval-specs.xlsx) — it includes the canonical doc list and labeling schema. For environment: we'd prefer hosted dedicated capacity for the initial eval, but can pivot to Private if needed for compliance.

Can we get a kickoff next week (Tue or Wed morning EST)?

Sara

Acme Corp
sara.patel@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Acme long-context eval — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Thanks Sara, good questions, answering inline: 

1) Latency examples
- Llama-3-70B-ctx (dedicated A100s, batching disabled for interactive path): p50 ~ 320ms for a ~3-token response on 8k prompt, ~420ms on 64k prompt; at 128k KV we surface ~480-650ms depending on KV cache warmness and kernel path. We'll include exact numbers in the bench run for your corpus.

2) Regression controls we run
- Baseline before quantization (fp16) -> compare to PTQ/INT8 variants across our eval set (we compute ROUGE/EM for extractive, BERTScore and citation-precision for summarization).
- We also run an automated hallucination detector (precision recall on labeled citations) and flag regression if citation precision drops >3 percentage points.
- If regressions appear, we propose either: a) different quantization (QLoRA/aware-PTQ), b) hybrid policy (fp16 for summarization routes, quantized for embeddings/rerank), or c) latency-tiered routing with fallback to fp16 for critical queries.

3) Truncation behavior
- Best practice is model-specific but we recommend: sliding-window + hierarchical summarization for extractive QA across chapters, prefix+KV for single-pass summarization. Our eval harness will run all three modes and show tradeoffs per metric.

Next steps / schedule
- We can run the initial 2-week eval on hosted dedicated capacity. Estimated turnaround for the first report: 7 business days after we receive the canonical corpus and access info.
- Lauren, can you confirm any constraints around canary policies and customer-facing SLA notes?
- Michael, can you prepare the quantization matrix we'll test (fp16, PTQ-8, PTQ-4 if stable) and the dedicated instance choices?

Sara, I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff Tue 11:00am EST unless you prefer Wed. Sending a calendar invite shortly.

Best,
Marissa
